column1: # Agent versions with a published security fix. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   id        what lines of the same tool share: they make one row in the report, which shows the hole
#             of each line the installed version falls under and says to update to the highest of
#             their fixed versions, or to a later fix when another line of the tool covers that one
#   name      as the report shows it
#   os        all, mac, linux or win (win is Git Bash and gird-check.ps1)
#   kind      plist   an Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString (an XML plist; a binary one is not read)
#             folder  the highest version-named folder in a folder
#             npm     a package's package.json in the global npm installs and npx's cache
#             mcparg  name@version in the MCP configs section 2 counts (not those in plugin catalogs and caches)
#   where     plist and folder: a path, with the path tokens of data/sessions.tsv or an absolute path.
#             npm and mcparg: the package name
#   affected  <fixed, or >=first <fixed, or >=first <=last for an advisory that names first to last and that no
#             version fixes. A version in that range gets a row of its own, under Tools with a published hole
#             and no fixed version yet: the version, no fixed version yet, and each such hole with its
#             advisory, naming no version to update to. It is kept apart from the fixes to install: row 01's
#             count, the fix to update and fleet mode's tools leave it out. A row with a fix that such a
#             line covers shows its hole as not fixed yet. A version past last has no row
#   hole      what the hole allows, a few words from the advisory
#   advisory  the advisory's https link
# Lines of one tool agree on its name, and lines of one advisory on its range and hole. Each tool has a
# line for its newest fix, and the version a row says to update to is never in another line's range with
# a fix, so it has no published fix of its own; an older advisory may have a line too, for what its hole
# allows.
# Versions compare part by part as numbers. A version that is not numbers and dots is not reported.
# Each tool's advisories were read in October 2026 from its vendor's repository, GitHub's global
# database and OSV: a repository can publish one that neither of the other two lists.
# Cursor is read on macOS only: its version file on the other systems was not verified. Its newest fix
# with a version is 3.1.2, for Cursor on macOS (GHSA-p9g2-cr55-cw9c, of the 33 advisories in
# cursor/cursor). Claude Code: anthropics/claude-code publishes 31 advisories for the npm package, and
# two of them are not in GitHub's global database; OSV has them only as CVE records, CVE-2026-103012 and
# CVE-2026-103435, outside its npm records. The newest fix is 2.1.260, from 2.0.68
# (GHSA-gfvf-j8jh-jxxw, one of the two); below 2.0.68 the highest fix is 2.1.179 (GHSA-pq7j-f95f-qfcv),
# in its range, so the row says 2.1.260 there too. GHSA-9f65-56v6-gxw7 and the sandbox escape
# GHSA-7835-87q9-rgvv have lines for what their holes allow. Claude Code's native installer keeps each
# version as a file in ~/.local/share/claude/versions and links ~/.local/bin/claude to the one in use
# (Claude Code's setup page): no kind reads that, and the highest version kept need not be the one in
# use. Claude Desktop: anthropics/claude-code also publishes four advisories for it. Its version is read on
# macOS only, from Claude.app's Info.plist as Cursor's is: its newest fix there is 1.15962.0
# (GHSA-v234-4jrq-mgg6, macOS), and GHSA-3rwf-2g6p-c2f9 has lines for its hole. No kind reads its version
# on Windows or Linux, so the two Windows advisories, GHSA-4p2j-qj3c-6x84 (below 1.8089.0) and
# GHSA-5p5x-5294-qhp3 (below 1.3834.0), have no line.
# mcp-remote: GHSA-6xpm-ggf7-wc3p is its only advisory with a fixed version, 0.1.16. GitHub's database also
# holds six unreviewed ones whose records carry no package or range field (their text gives the range), so
# ?affects= does not find them, and none names a fix; OSV gives each only a last affected commit, and the
# repository (now punkpeye/mcp-remote) publishes no advisory and no release note that names one. Five come
# from one researcher's review of 0.1.16 to 0.1.38 (playb0t/mcp-remote-oauth-security, v1.0.1, whose
# write-ups claim less than the advisories' text), and GHSA-jrvg-vw6c-rp59 covers 0.8.0 to 0.14.3. Each one
# whose write-up shows a hole has a line with no fixed version for the range its text gives, and its hole
# says what the write-up shows:
#   GHSA-v65w-6crh-cp3h (CVE-2026-51997, high), 0.1.16 to 0.1.38: F-08, a hostile authorization endpoint
#     opening an internal address in the browser (its text says code execution);
#   GHSA-mvq8-g2rm-4rhm (CVE-2026-51996, critical), 0.1.16 to 0.1.38: F-04, MD5 keeping each server's token
#     files apart, with no token takeover or real-token access demonstrated (its text says code execution);
#   GHSA-8rrr-xx35-4q6h (CVE-2026-51994, critical), 0.1.32 to 0.1.38: F-01, the resource_metadata URL a
#     hostile server sends fetched with no address policy, which a localhost canary showed reaching local
#     services;
#   GHSA-5wmf-76f4-cg47 (CVE-2026-51995, high), 0.1.32 to 0.1.38: F-02, the authorization server origin a
#     hostile server names fetched unchecked, blind probing of internal services (its text says it leaks
#     sensitive information; no response was read out);
#   GHSA-jrvg-vw6c-rp59 (CVE-2026-108716, medium), 0.8.0 to 0.14.3: its write-up (HaiND's, on hackmd) shows
#     --device-code sending the client secret and tokens to whatever endpoints the server's metadata names,
#     with no HTTPS check.
# GHSA-4gh6-j99c-x6g2 (CVE-2026-52001, high, 0.1.18 to 0.1.38) has no line: its write-up, F-11, says the
# SDK's origin check and undici's redirect handling refute its token-forwarding claim, calls it defense in
# depth and claims no CVE. The code each line names is the same in 0.15.2, the newest on npm (20 October
# 2026): the browser URL is opened after only sanitizeUrl, which checks the protocol; MD5 still names the
# token files; the resource_metadata URL and the first authorization server are fetched unchecked; and
# device-authorization.ts is unchanged since 0.14.3 (0.14.4 changed only the OAuth error page). So no
# version is named for them: a version in one of these ranges is a tool with a published hole and no fixed
# version yet, and the row of a version below 0.1.16 says to update to 0.1.16 for the command injection
# and that no version fixes the two that cover 0.1.16. A version past a range has no row for that
# advisory: its text covers only that range.
# Amazon Q: the version folder is the language server's (Language Servers for AWS), which the bulletin
# fixes in 1.69.0 (aws/language-servers publishes the bulletin's two advisories, and no later bulletin
# names it). The extension's own version is not read. Amazon Q keeps the server in
# aws/toolkits/language-servers/AmazonQ under ~/Library/Caches, ~/.cache or %LOCALAPPDATA%: so says
# its own code, Amazon-Q-Developer/amazon-q-vscode, which the 2.8.0 extension names as its source, and
# so does that build. The aws/language-servers/<name> folder of aws-toolkit-vscode is the AWS
# Toolkit's own.
# id
